classifications.reason: AuditLog is immutable evidence already protected by the #562 delete guard during tenant cascades.
classifications.recovery: Tenant deletion must use the lifecycle authority; failed cascades roll back atomically and retained audit remains restorable.

classifications.reason: FX ledger snapshots are accounting evidence and must not disappear when a ledger line is deleted.
classifications.recovery: Preserve the snapshot and require an explicit accounting recovery or reversal before any parent cleanup.

classifications.reason: Tenant deletion must not silently erase historical FX ledger evidence.
classifications.recovery: Tenant offboarding remains blocked until retained accounting evidence is handled by the lifecycle authority.

classifications.reason: Fiscal close evidence is immutable and already protected by #562 during tenant deletion.
classifications.recovery: A blocked tenant delete rolls back; close evidence remains available for export and controlled recovery.

classifications.reason: Issued fiscal documents are immutable under #562 and tenant cascades are intercepted by the lifecycle guard.
classifications.recovery: A blocked cascade rolls back and fiscal documents remain recoverable under the documented tenant lifecycle workflow.

classifications.reason: Rule snapshots prove which fiscal rule produced an issued document and cannot be removed by tenant cascade.
classifications.recovery: Keep snapshots with fiscal evidence; recovery restores the retained snapshot alongside its referenced document.

classifications.reason: Versioned fiscal rules are historical authority and must survive generic tenant deletion attempts.
classifications.recovery: Retain rule versions until a separately authorized lifecycle policy permits archival or purge.

classifications.reason: Fiscal numbering state is an auditable authority and accidental tenant cascade can create numbering reuse risk.
classifications.recovery: Keep sequence state through offboarding so recovery cannot reissue historical fiscal numbers.

classifications.reason: LedgerEntry is immutable accounting history already protected by #562 and ledger lifecycle guards.
classifications.recovery: Tenant delete attempts roll back while ledger history remains available for export, restore, and compensating entries.

classifications.reason: LedgerLine is structurally owned by LedgerEntry; parent deletion is itself fail-closed for retained or posted history.
classifications.recovery: Lines recover with their parent aggregate; posted entries use reversal rather than destructive parent deletion.

classifications.reason: Legal acceptance evidence must not be erased as a side effect of deleting a tenant.
classifications.recovery: Retain acceptance evidence until an explicit legal/privacy lifecycle workflow authorizes disposition.

classifications.reason: Deleting a user must not silently erase evidence of accepted legal document versions.
classifications.recovery: Preserve acceptance evidence independently of account deactivation/deletion until approved disposition.

classifications.reason: TaxDeclaration is a structural child of TaxPeriod; #685 makes the parent itself fail-closed for destructive lifecycle operations.
classifications.recovery: Declarations recover with the retained TaxPeriod aggregate; no cascade can start while the parent guard denies deletion.

classifications.reason: Tax periods currently cascade from Tenant without the #562 protected-entity guard used by other fiscal history.
classifications.recovery: The new immutable lifecycle policy blocks deletion and causes the whole tenant cascade transaction to roll back.

classifications.reason: Budget Wallet audit journal history must not be erased automatically when its auth owner is deleted.
classifications.recovery: Account cleanup is blocked until audit retention/disposition is explicitly handled, preserving journal evidence.

classifications.reason: Hípico audit events are operational evidence and must not vanish when the auth owner is deleted.
classifications.recovery: Owner deletion remains blocked while audit evidence exists; export or authorized disposition must occur first.

classifications.reason: Workspace cleanup may proceed without destroying audit events because workspace_id is nullable evidence context.
classifications.recovery: Audit events survive workspace deletion; remaining owner and payload evidence support historical reconstruction.
